description: Registry of debate transcripts and candidate datasets for ARGUMAP research, annotation, and benchmarking. Captures provenance, native label schemes, licensing, and intended project roles. Licenses and clearance states are strictly verified against authoritative legal and institutional sources. Speculative licenses are rejected or designated as UNVERIFIED. Datasets cannot be cleared for model training without explicit primary evidence.

datasets.name: UK House of Lords Hansard (Advanced Artificial Intelligence Debate 2023)
datasets.paper: Official Report (Hansard), UK House of Lords, Vol. 832, 24 July 2023
datasets.dialogue_structure: Full verbatim House of Lords chamber debate across 29 turns and 28 speakers with structured motions, questions, cross-bench arguments, and ministerial replies.
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Verbatim transcript retrieved directly from official UK Parliament Hansard REST API. Open Parliament Licence v3.0 explicitly permits commercial and non-commercial reproduction, adaptation, and model training with mandatory attribution.
datasets.training_clearance_evidence: https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/copyright-parliament/open-parliament-licence/ (Open Parliament Licence v3.0 terms verified; Hansard Debate ExtId 5432715E-F305-4EC1-8A79-B9A0C6402BFF)
datasets.attribution: Contains Parliamentary information licensed under the Open Parliament Licence v3.0.
datasets.intended_use: Verified replacement for debate_001. Raw text is cleared; supervised model training remains gated until human annotations adhering to guideline v1.0.0 are completed and validated as gold.
datasets.notes: Authentic verbatim transcript ingested from official UK Parliament Hansard API. Licensed under Open Parliament Licence v3.0 with attribution: 'Contains Parliamentary information licensed under the Open Parliament Licence v3.0.'. Gated from supervised model training until full annotation pipeline produces validated gold data.

datasets.name: UK House of Commons Hansard (AI & Workforce Automation Debate 2024 - Legacy Synthetic Pilot)
datasets.paper: Official Report (Hansard), UK House of Commons, 2024
datasets.dialogue_structure: Formal parliamentary floor debate with procedural interventions, questions, and ministerial responses.
datasets.license: UNVERIFIED (Adapted/Curated Demonstration Dialogue; Purported OPL v3.0)
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Audit reveals local raw file is an adapted/curated demonstration debate not found in verbatim Hansard (Dr. Sarah Wollaston was not an MP in 2024). OPL v3.0 applies only to genuine Parliamentary Information published by Parliament. Blocked pending documentation of true authorial provenance or replacement with verified verbatim Hansard speech.
datasets.training_clearance_evidence: https://hansard.parliament.uk/ (Official Hansard records show no 2024 speech by Dr. Sarah Wollaston; text is unverified synthetic/curated dialogue)
datasets.intended_use: Legacy pilot annotation demonstration: Archived under data/annotations/legacy_synthetic/. Model training permanently BLOCKED.
datasets.notes: Official UK Parliament Hansard is published under Open Parliament Licence v3.0 (OPL v3.0). However, the specific text stored in data/raw/other/uk_hansard_ai_debate_2024.txt is an adapted demonstration dialogue that does not match verbatim official Hansard records (Dr. Sarah Wollaston was not in Parliament in 2024). Thus, OPL v3.0 clearance cannot be verified for the local file. Superseded by uk_hansard_lords_2023.

datasets.name: 1960 First Kennedy-Nixon Presidential Debate (U.S. Senate Official Records)
datasets.paper: Freedom of Communications: Final Report of the Committee on Commerce, U.S. Senate (S. Rep. No. 994, Part III, 87th Cong., 1st Sess., 1961)
datasets.dialogue_structure: Formal presidential debate with opening statements, cross-candidate questions, and counter-arguments.
datasets.training_clearance_reason: 1960 presidential campaign debate speeches and commercial network broadcasts (CBS/NBC/ABC) are not works of the United States Government under 17 U.S.C. § 105. Republication in S. Rep. No. 994 does not extinguish underlying rights (Compendium of U.S. Copyright Office Practices § 313.6(C)(2)). Furthermore, local raw text contains adapted wording and factual errors ('Governor Nixon' vs 'Mr. Nixon'). Blocked pending legal copyright determination and replacement with verified verbatim transcript.
datasets.training_clearance_evidence: 17 U.S.C. § 101/105; Compendium of U.S. Copyright Office Practices § 313.6(C)(2); S. Rep. No. 994, Part III (1961)
datasets.intended_use: Primary pilot annotation: Historical adversarial debate structure. Model training BLOCKED pending legal review of broadcast rights and transcript verification.
datasets.notes: While reprinted in U.S. Senate S. Rep. No. 994, political campaign debates are not works prepared by federal employees as part of official duties under 17 U.S.C. § 105. Broadcast copyright belonged to commercial networks (CBS), and candidate speeches held common law copyright under the 1909 Act. The local raw file is also an adapted/condensed excerpt. Public domain status cannot be verified from archive reprinting alone.

datasets.name: US2016 Presidential Debates Corpus (AIFdb / CPD Excerpt)
datasets.paper: Visser et al. (2019) / Menini et al. (2018). Never Retreat, Never Explain: A Corpus of 2016 US Presidential Debates. AAAI 2018.
datasets.domain: Televised Political Debates (2016 US General Election)
datasets.dialogue_structure: Two-candidate podium debate with moderator questions, direct rebuttals, and cross-talk.
datasets.license: UNVERIFIED (Academic Fair Use / CPD Copyright Pending)
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Commission on Presidential Debates (CPD) asserts proprietary copyright over presidential debate broadcasts and transcripts. Research annotation permitted locally under 17 U.S.C. § 107 fair use, but downstream public release of fine-tuned models or trained weights is blocked without explicit rights or substitution.
datasets.intended_use: Pilot Annotation & Reference: Rich real-world political clash. Model training BLOCKED pending legal clarification.
datasets.notes: Commission on Presidential Debates (CPD) asserts copyright over official broadcast debate transcripts. While non-commercial research use of excerpts is supported under U.S. fair use (17 U.S.C. § 107) and AIFdb academic sharing terms, public distribution of trained weights or raw transcripts requires legal review or switching to a public-domain transcript source (e.g. UCSB American Presidency Project).

datasets.name: QT30 (BBC Question Time Corpus)
datasets.paper: Visser et al. (2020) / Hautli-Janisz et al. (2022). QT30: A Corpus of Argument and Conflict in Broadcast Debate. Proceedings of LREC 2022.
datasets.dialogue_structure: Turn-taking multi-party television debate with host, panel, and audience questions.
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Not downloaded. CC BY-NC 4.0 permits non-commercial academic research, but strictly blocks commercial model training. Requires evaluation prior to download.
datasets.training_clearance_evidence: https://corpora.aifdb.org/qt30; Hautli-Janisz et al. (LREC 2022); Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International
datasets.intended_use: Candidate external data source: Multi-party panel deliberation for non-commercial research evaluation.
datasets.notes: Released under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International (CC BY-NC 4.0) via AIFdb. Permitted for non-commercial academic research. Commercial use strictly prohibited.

datasets.name: ElecDeb60To20 (US Presidential Debates 1960-2020)
datasets.paper: Haddad et al. (2021). 60 Years of US Presidential Debates: A Multi-Modal Dataset. Findings of EMNLP 2021.
datasets.dialogue_structure: Formal political debate transcripts partitioned by speaker turns and time codes.
datasets.training_clearance_reason: The NoDerivatives (ND) clause of CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 strictly prohibits distributing modified, re-tokenized, or re-annotated derivative datasets or fine-tuned model weights.
datasets.intended_use: Read-only comparative baseline: Evaluating debate unit density. Ineligible for derivative redistribution.
datasets.notes: Distributed on Hugging Face under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). RESTRICTION: The NoDerivatives (ND) clause prohibits redistributing modified, re-annotated, or converted versions of the corpus.

datasets.name: M-Arg (Multimodal Argumentation Dataset)
datasets.paper: Mancini et al. (2022). M-Arg: Multimodal Argument Mining Dataset. Proceedings of LREC 2022.
datasets.dialogue_structure: Competitive parliamentary and academic debate speeches.
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Not downloaded. Underlying debate transcripts reported as CC0/public domain; annotation layer CC-BY. Requires primary source ingestion and unit boundary verification before inclusion.
datasets.intended_use: Auxiliary comparative reference: Evaluating debate argument density and speech-to-unit segmentation.
datasets.notes: Underlying presidential debate transcripts derived from public domain Kaggle election records (CC0 1.0); research annotation repository shared under CC-BY open science terms.

datasets.name: AbstRCT (Randomized Clinical Trial Abstracts)
datasets.paper: Mayer et al. (2020). Enhancing Argument Mining in Medical Abstracts. Proceedings of EMNLP 2020.
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Not downloaded. ShareAlike (SA) clause requires any derivative dataset or model to be shared under identical terms. Non-dialogic clinical trial abstract domain.
datasets.intended_use: Auxiliary reference: Linguistic indicators distinguishing empirical scientific evidence from conclusory claims.
datasets.notes: Explicitly licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) on GitLab. Permitted for non-commercial research; derivative annotations must be shared under identical terms.

datasets.name: Arg-Microtexts Corpus
datasets.paper: Peldszus and Stede (2015). An Annotated Corpus of Argumentative Microtexts. First Workshop on Argumentation Mining.
datasets.domain: Short Controlled Editorial Texts (German & English translations)
datasets.dialogue_structure: Short controlled monologues (typically 5 argumentative propositions per text).
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Not downloaded. ShareAlike non-commercial license. Monologue texts, non-conversational.
datasets.intended_use: Auxiliary structural reference: Verification of tree and graph structural properties (DAG vs cyclic structures).
datasets.notes: Explicitly licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) on GitHub. Non-commercial academic research use only.

datasets.name: Argument Annotated Essays (AAE v2)
datasets.paper: Stab and Gurevych (2017). Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays. Computational Linguistics 43(3).
datasets.license: UNVERIFIED (TUdatalib Custom Academic Terms / ACL CC BY-NC-SA)
datasets.training_clearance_reason: TUdatalib repository access terms unverified for redistribution of derivative annotations.
datasets.intended_use: Auxiliary benchmark: Evaluation of proposition boundary segmentation and baseline premise/claim classification.
datasets.notes: Published on TUdatalib institutional repository under custom institutional research terms. Paper in ACL Anthology under CC BY-NC-SA. Retained as UNVERIFIED pending verification of specific TUdatalib redistribution conditions.

datasets.name: IBM Debater - Evidence Sentence Detection
datasets.paper: Rinott et al. (2015). Show Me Your Evidence - An Extractive Approach to Argumentative Evidence Detection. Proceedings of EMNLP 2015.
datasets.domain: Wikipedia Articles across 58 Controversial Debate Topics
datasets.dialogue_structure: Extracted sentence candidates matched to topic queries.
datasets.license: UNVERIFIED (IBM Research / CC BY-SA 3.0 Wikipedia text)
datasets.training_clearance_reason: Custom click-through academic terms unverified for external redistribution.
datasets.intended_use: Auxiliary reference: Fine-grained subtype definitions for the EVIDENCE component class.
datasets.notes: Underlying Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 3.0; compiled evidence annotations released under IBM Project Debater research terms. Retained as UNVERIFIED pending formal review of IBM end-user terms.

datasets.intended_use: Auxiliary comparative reference: Evaluating informal user rebuttals and counter-positions.
datasets.notes: Text compiled from third-party public web forums. License terms unverified from primary source; marked UNVERIFIED pending copyright clearance of forum user comments.
